headline: Oil Rebounds Strongly as Middle East Realities Reassert Themselves
paragraphs: Crude oil staged a sharp recovery on Friday, with Brent jumping 5.62 percent to EUR 89.14 and WTI climbing 4.07 percent to EUR 81.80 following a brutal midweek rout. Headlines attribute this rebound to Mideast war realities reemerging and markets mulling over prospects for a Middle East settlement, though crude still finished the week deeply in the red after diving on earlier signs of a glut and post-midterm election reactions.

Precious metals also saw notable upward momentum ahead of the United States Non-Farm Payrolls jobs report. Platinum gained 1.51 percent to EUR 1358.99 and palladium surged 3.17 percent to EUR 919.99, reclaiming the one thousand dollar threshold amid strong weekly gains across the precious complex, while gold held firmly above four thousand dollars.
The euro traded at 1.1212 against the US dollar, influencing euro-denominated commodity costs. Movement drivers for natural gas and silver were not specified in the available news data.
